name: audit-dependency-hygiene
title: Dependency hygiene for npm and transitive pins
description: Every third-party fetch this repo owns is deliberate and reviewed. The Python dev toolchain becomes hash-locked and wheel-only; no npm lifecycle script runs un-reviewed. Scope narrowed 2026-08-10: the `npx --yes repomix` docs refresh keeps an unlocked transitive tree, recorded as an accepted risk rather than solved with a vendored npm lockfile, and `.opencode/package.json` is upstream-Trellis vendored so its floating dependency is recorded, not removed. See prd.md for the exact boundary.
creator: sdelmas
notes: Scheduled (order 110) by 08-08-trellis-backlog-hygiene on 2026-08-09: deliberately deferred audit follow-up, kept actionable in the autonomous backlog rather than parked or archived; see .trellis/tasks/archive/2026-08/08-08-trellis-backlog-hygiene/record.md (that task has since been archived; the order-110 entry is at :74). Planning converged 2026-08-10 and escalated from PRD-only to prd+design+implement. Ownership split settled that day by the two lookups in .trellis/spec/backend/quality-guidelines.md:772-784: .opencode/package.json is upstream-Trellis vendored (Registry A hit, Registry B absent, templateReceipted in .github/trellis-provenance.json), so A-032 becomes a four-field local-only record plus a CONTRIBUTING.md:78 correction and no local edit; A-033 and A-034 sit on repo-owned files and get real changes. Write set: requirements-dev.lock (new, generated by `make lock`), requirements-dev.txt (header comment), .github/scripts/check-dev-requirements-lock.py (new) and tests/test_dev_requirements_lock.py, .github/trellis-provenance.json (regenerated -- a new tracked .github file is an `uncovered:` finding until absorbed with --write --accept), Makefile, .github/workflows/tests.yml, .sd-ai-command-pack/check.json, scripts/update_repomix, tests/test_repomix.py, README.md (accepted-risk note), CONTRIBUTING.md, .trellis/spec/backend/quality-guidelines.md. Measured 2026-08-10: 4 direct pins plus 6 floating transitives, all via mypy = 10 locked entries; drift is live (ast-serialize 0.6.0 installed vs 0.8.0 resolved under an unchanged mypy==2.3.0). Codex round 1 raised 9 concerns (7 blocking), all dispositioned; the npm transitive tree stays unlocked as a recorded accepted risk, which narrows the original goal deliberately.
